current_answer: People have built games, browser demos, desktop apps, art, brain engines and research tests on real fruit fly connectomes, mainly FlyWire (female brain) and MaleCNS (male brain and nerve cord). We checked 121 of them on 8 October 2026: 44 can be opened in a browser or free notebook without installing anything (in our browser checks of 3 and 6 Oct 2026, 8 of 11 demos ran on a machine without a GPU). Is it a brain or just a map? It is a map of one fly's wiring (a fly brain scan) run with a simple neuron model, and in our own pre-registered tests that wiring made a difference. We ran the map. A looming shadow on one eye turned our simulated fly away in 6 of 6 runs. With the same map scrambled (same number of connections per neuron) it turned away in 0 of 3. Here the map's wiring, not the stimulus or our code, makes the turn. (5 and 8 Oct 2026; left eye 3 of 3, right eye 3 of 3; the body walks with FlyGym's own controller through our hand-made mapping.) With the escape neuron silenced, the fly still turned away. With only the inside of the map scrambled, the fly turned away in 0 of 6 runs. In brain-only follow-ups: We turned the scrambled maps up until they were as busy as the real one. They still did not produce the turn: the wiring, not the amount of activity, makes it. (6 Oct) How strong must the shadow be? (8 Oct) We lowered the input to the looming neurons step by step, from 80 to 10 spikes per second each. The turn command appeared from about 30 per second (38% of our strongest input) on both sides; below that the model did not turn. The escape neuron started firing at the same input as the turn command. A second random seed agreed. With one relay neuron (PVLP141) silenced, the turn command stayed. With all 21-23 relay neurons between the looming neurons and the turn neuron silenced, the turn command stayed. 'Stayed' means the pre-registered turn rule still passed; the ratio we used saturates because the near-side turn neuron is always at 0 Hz, and with PVLP141 silenced the far-side turn-neuron rate did fall (left 25 to 17 Hz, right 41 to 24 Hz); a disclosure, not a new reading. Caveat: One model (Shiu et al. LIF on FlyWire v783), brain only; the input is a rate we set for every LC4/LPLC2 of one eye, not a measured response to a real shadow; 'silenced' means the neuron's output synapses were removed; not a real fly. We found no measured real-fly LC4/LPLC2 firing rate to compare against. A coupled brain-and-body test is not yet tested. The 'away' direction rests on our mapping and fly67's claim. Is it AI? The base model is not trained AI: it copies the wiring and sets one strength by hand; of 87 graded projects, 48 add a trained, learning or search-tuned part in the main path (catalogue field trained_class). Can it suffer? We found no study that measured consciousness or suffering in these models; fly larvae detect harmful heat and pressure, and whether flies feel pain is open. Can I put it in my game? Yes for a non-commercial project with credit, in our cautious reading of FlyWire's CC BY-NC 4.0 (its Zenodo record says CC BY 4.0; not legal advice); MaleCNS is CC BY 4.0. What do I have to download? Two files, 104.1 MB, to run the brain model; FlyWire v783 in full is 10.6 GB, MaleCNS 31.3 GB, BANC 536.1 GB. Most viral demos really run a simulated fly brain, but a person chose which neurons receive the input and which neurons act, and several get most of their movement from scripts or trained parts; no fly has been "uploaded". The newest claim, "Can A Conscious Fly Brain Learn how to Hack?" by dzuma (approximately 37,310 views on 8 Oct 2026, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m5Q_aIO_K8o), links no code and is graded U; all 21 verdicts were re-checked (13 with code unchanged since graded, 8 with no code). Does the real fly wiring help? Sometimes: across 43 control studies it beat scrambled wiring in 16 of 34, mostly untrained reflex, sensory and steering circuits; in trained, reservoir, ML, game, robot-arm and our walking tests it tied or lost (10). Across 23 studies with a no-brain baseline the fly network beats it in only 4; in Doom a brainless autopilot survives 51.93 s against the fly brain's 53.34 s (doom-fly-control by gabrycina), and in our walking test a scrambled brain and no brain walked the FlyGym fly as far as the real brain. A beginner can run the published whole-brain model on a CPU: in our test on 2 CPUs sugar input drove MN9 to 85.2 Hz and shuffled wiring dropped it to 0 Hz; re-tested 5 Oct 2026 (6 of 6 tests, 82.0 Hz bit-exact), with tested deeper steps for a FlyGym body and a looming sense. Brain (Brian2 2.9.0) and body (FlyGym 2.1.0) installed together in one Python 3.12 environment: 1.1 GB on disk, tested 8 Oct 2026, with numpy pinned to 2.3.5 (Brian2 2.9.0 does not import with numpy 2.5.3). A 20-minute Use in class plan is on Build your own.

catalogue_card.question: What have people built with the digital fruit fly brain, and what is real?
catalogue_card.text: 121 fruit fly brain simulation projects checked in code, each marked for trained parts (is it AI?): 44 you can try online, 55 videos with evidence grades, verdicts on 21 viral claims, 43 control studies, and our own tests: in the brain model the looming turn command appeared from about 30 spikes per second per looming neuron (brain only, one model, an input rate we set; not a real fly).

summary: 121 entries checked on 8 Oct 2026 (5 new in the tenth check): 27 grade A, 25 B, 31 C, 4 D, 10 U and 24 datasets or tools (not graded). trained_class: 48 of 87 graded projects have a trained, learning or search-tuned part in the main path, 39 have none.

How strong must the shadow be? (made by us, brain only, pre-registered at 09:45:48 UTC on 8 Oct 2026 before the first trial; 19 trials): We lowered the input to the looming neurons step by step, from 80 to 10 spikes per second each. The turn command appeared from about 30 per second (38% of our strongest input) on both sides; below that the model did not turn. The escape neuron started firing at the same input as the turn command. Reading: "moderate"; escape order "together"; a second seed agreed ("stable across seeds"). With one relay neuron (PVLP141) silenced, the turn command stayed. With all 21-23 relay neurons between the looming neurons and the turn neuron silenced, the turn command stayed. 'Stayed' means the pre-registered turn rule still passed; the ratio we used saturates because the near-side turn neuron is always at 0 Hz, and with PVLP141 silenced the far-side turn-neuron rate did fall (left 25 to 17 Hz, right 41 to 24 Hz); a disclosure, not a new reading. One model (Shiu et al. LIF on FlyWire v783), brain only; the input is a rate we set for every LC4/LPLC2 of one eye, not a measured response to a real shadow; 'silenced' means the neuron's output synapses were removed; not a real fly. We found no measured real-fly LC4/LPLC2 rate to compare against.

Where in the wiring is the turn? (6 Oct 2026; made by us, brain only, pre-registered at 09:42:54 UTC on 6 Oct 2026 before the first trial; 22 new trials with a faster input that passed its pre-registered check): We turned the scrambled maps up until they were as busy as the real one. They still did not produce the turn: the wiring, not the amount of activity, makes it. 3 of 3 shuffles matched the real activity (gain 2.25, 0.98 x real outside the stimulated cells) and all gave a 0 Hz turn command. Inside-only scramble: Scrambling only the inside of the map kept about -9% of the turn command and 69% of the escape signal. (-9% means none: the far-side command was absent in all 6 trials; descriptive, not pre-registered: the near-side giant fibre kept 151-169 Hz, the far side went to 0). With the escape neuron silenced, the turn command stayed. (2 of 2; expected, as the map has no giant fibre to DNa02 connections). Census: no direct looming-to-DNa02 synapses; top relay PVLP141. Brain only: 7 drives await body runs.

We ran the map (5 and 8 Oct 2026, pre-registered): We ran the map. A looming shadow on one eye turned our simulated fly away in 6 of 6 runs. With the same map scrambled (same number of connections per neuron) it turned away in 0 of 3. Here the map's wiring, not the stimulus or our code, makes the turn. Left eye 3 of 3, right eye 3 of 3; the 5 Oct floor run repeated exactly on 8 Oct. With the escape neuron silenced, the fly still turned away (2 of 2). With only the inside of the map scrambled, the fly turned away in 0 of 6 runs. One model, open loop, our hand-made mapping, a constant external walking drive, 1 s; the body walks with FlyGym's controller; not a real fly. fly67 stays grade B.

Plain answers with evidence on Is it real?: Is it AI? (the base model is not trained AI; 48 of 87 graded projects add trained, learning or tuned parts); Is it a brain or just a map? (a map run with a simple model; in our tests its wiring drove a reflex and a turn, body software did the walking); Can it suffer? (no study measured suffering in these models; whether flies feel pain is open); Can I put it in my game? (yes for non-commercial projects with credit, our cautious reading of CC BY-NC 4.0; not legal advice); new: What do I have to download? (two files, 104.1 MB, for the beginner path).

Controls ledger (8 Oct 2026): 43 studies, 34 with a wiring null: helps 16, no difference 8, worse 2, mixed 7, not yet scored 1. New: Connectocopter (helps: 15 of 15 looming escapes against 0 of 15 rewired, but a hand-written controller also escapes 15 of 15; unfair, weak) and Synaptera (baselines only by the fixed rules). Our looming row: real n 6 and an inside-only arm, still fair and strong. Convention: extraction files with results_in_repo_files false means the numbers come only from a README. No scoring rule changed.
Our walking test (2 Oct): real brain 13.93 mm, scrambled 14.15 mm, brainless constant drive 14.28 mm in 1 s; the legs are FlyGym's, and our mapping capped the drive.

Our 1 Oct fair test on the sugar reflex: real wiring 85.2 ± 3.56 Hz; degree-preserving and weight shuffles 0 Hz; boundary-preserving 39 Hz (retention 0.46); sign shuffle 214 Hz with the whole brain ignited. The gain-matched arm was not matched on 3 shuffles; the row stays mixed, unfair and weak.

Where the wiring helps, a brain-free baseline often matches the fly anyway: the fly network beats a no-brain baseline in only 4 of 23 studies. In Doom (doom-fly-control by gabrycina) the fly survives 53.34 s, shuffled wiring 6.75 s and a brainless autopilot 51.93 s.

Build your own: tested 28 Sep 2026 on Linux with 2 CPUs (MN9 85.2 Hz real, 0 Hz shuffled) and re-tested 5 Oct 2026 (6 of 6 tests, 82.0 Hz bit-exact). Tested deeper steps: Add a body (2 Oct, FlyGym 2.1.0, our mapping), Add a sense: looming (5 Oct), and brain and body in one Python 3.12 environment (8 Oct: 1.1 GB on disk, numpy pinned to 2.3.5; with numpy 2.5.3, import brian2 fails with AttributeError: type object 'numpy.ndarray' has no attribute 'ptp'). Use in class: a 20-minute plan with play.drosophila.io as an alternative.

Does it actually run? (our browser checks of 3 and 6 Oct 2026, headless Chromium 154, Linux, no GPU; not a play test): 8 of 11 demos ran. 6 Oct: Vial 7.43 MB, Doodle Fly 34.99 MB and Infinite Sugar 36.04 MB ran computing in your browser, Fly Dino 3.81 MB ran, and Neural Canvas ran but its ~77 MB brain download was not seen in our check window. 3 Oct: Fly Worker, FLY67 and flybrain.app ran; FlyLeno and Help the Fly Escape froze after loading; fly-brain (Lulzx) stopped at our 1.6 GB memory limit. No demo computed on a server.
New entries (8 Oct 2026): Connectocopter (A), Synaptera (B), Fly Brain Tetris (B), fly-jumpshot (C) and the dzuma "learns to hack" video claim (U, no code).

"Can A Conscious Fly Brain Learn how to Hack?" by dzuma (approximately 37,310 views on 8 Oct 2026, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m5Q_aIO_K8o): no code linked, grade U. "I Taught a Fly How to Play Gorilla Tag (seriously)" (approximately 928,414 views on 8 Oct 2026, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wK4lixw7p4M) still names no code: U.
Video gallery (8 Oct 2026): 55 videos (52 English, 2 Russian, 1 Spanish); the dzuma claim video added; all available. View counts are approximate snapshots with their date. Thumbnails unchanged.

Download facts (6 Oct 2026, from hosts' storage metadata, no data downloaded): the beginner path needs Connectivity_783.parquet (100,804,642 B) and Completeness_783.csv (3,327,347 B); FlyWire v783 on Zenodo 10.6 GB in 5 files, MaleCNS v1.0 31.3 GB in 11 files, BANC 536.1 GB in 379 files (308.3 GB on request). MANC and larva L1 sizes are not stated.
"91%" is the share of 164 testable predictions of the brain-only Shiu et al. 2024 model that matched experiments; "95%" compares versions of the model and is not an accuracy.
FlyWire data is CC BY-NC 4.0 in FlyWire's guidelines (non-commercial; the Zenodo v783 record says CC BY 4.0, and we follow the stricter reading); MaleCNS, MANC, hemibrain and BANC data are CC BY.
uncertainty: Our looming tests: one model (Shiu et al. LIF on FlyWire v783), our hand-made mapping, an input we set (every LC4 and LPLC2 of one eye at a fixed rate for 1 s); not a real fly. Body (5 and 8 Oct): 6 real runs and 3 scrambled body runs with identical drives; 3 more scrambled and 5 inside-only drives equal the no-brain floor and take its walk by determinism (the floor run repeated exactly). Brain only (6 Oct): n 6 real, 6 plain scramble, 3 turned-up scramble, 6 inside-only, 2 giant fibre off. Brain only (8 Oct): one input series per eye (seed 2) and 4 second-seed checks; the relay readings rest on a ratio that saturates when the near side is silent (the far-side rate fell with PVLP141 silenced); no measured real-fly LC4/LPLC2 rate was found to compare with. The 'away' direction rests on our mapping's DNa02 sign and fly67's claim.

The plain answers rest on our reading of project files (trained_class), one primary nociception source, hosts' storage metadata for download sizes and our licence reading, which is not legal advice; whether CC BY or CC BY-NC applies to a FlyWire release is an open question with FlyWire.

Our body test covers one stimulus (P9 at 150 Hz on both sides), one brain model, one body, 1 s of open-loop walking, 3 trial seeds and 3 shuffles that sent identical drives. The rate-to-drive mapping is ours: it caps the drive at 1.2, so another mapping could let the wiring matter more. The pre-registered P9 sign, other P9 rates and other descending neuron types were not tested in the body.

Our fair test covers one reflex (sugar to MN9) in one model, with one 1 s trial per shuffle at one trial seed; the MN9 rate cannot tell selective drive from global ignition. The gain-matched arm is not matched on 3 shuffles; a per-shuffle gain search has not been run.

Browser checks (3 and 6 Oct): one headless Chromium 154 on Linux without a GPU, 60-90 s per demo, one action each; not a play test. Both freezes most likely come from software WebGL on our machine; GPU machines, Safari, Firefox and phones were not tested. Activity detection is coarse (screenshots every 5 s), bytes cover only the first 60-90 s, and traffic in cross-origin frames is not counted. Protocol completions and three deviations (a tool bug fixed and re-run within the 2-load limit) were written down but not pre-registered by the planner. View counts come from YouTube search pages; the Terraria, Gorilla Tag and Roblox fight videos were not watched. Neural Canvas's ~77 MB brain download was not seen in our 6 Oct window; where Fly Dino and Neural Canvas compute is unclear by our fixed rule.
The Terraria verdict rests on code older than the video; fly-walking-wiring's B is provisional because its results are not public. The Flyhard match of the driving compilation rests on one thumbnail.

Controls ledger: every number except our own three tests is the authors'. We recomputed 18 studies from their committed files but re-ran none; none is replicated, and only 2 of 43 are peer-reviewed. Only 13 of 43 studies reach "strong" method quality; 24 are weak. Fly-Racer and FlyBrain Flappy rest on README numbers; fly tennis rests on one match per condition. Synaptera's class follows the fixed rules; we did not inspect its shuffle method. Connectocopter's baseline arm is read from its README.

Ledger labels (wiring effect, fairness, quality) come from fixed yes/no rules applied to code and files; they are consistent but coarse. Our body test scores strong although its 3 shuffles behaved as one; our reflex test is "mixed" by rule although its arms read silent, partly and runaway. We did not override the rules for our own rows. Activity fields are reported only for our two tests. Retention puts very different measurements on one scale. The flyvis ablation values exist only in a figure and were not extracted; our text search of its supplement was crude (no PDF tool).

The "helps" results are mostly one kind of test (does a reflex pathway still carry signal after rewiring?), which is a low bar; boundary-preserving nulls have been applied to one reflex (ours: 46% kept), not to the other reflex studies.

Borderline grades: FlyLeno (B, borderline C); Fly Worker, fly-brain by Lulzx, The Fly's Hash Function, Fly OCR, Fly Self Driving, the null-model study and fly-brain-zero-shot are borderline A; fly-brain by erojas and Kick the Fly could argue B; acamilo-flybrain would sit on the B/C border without its stream macros.

Several C grades and the fafbseg entry rest on file citations that we spot-read but did not re-verify line by line. fly-plays-games runs its neurons in an external package (fly.ai) that we did not inspect beyond its commit subjects.

The Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim are known only through news articles, a Reddit post and a Twitch page read through summarising tools or search summaries; X, TikTok and Reddit cannot be searched without a login.

Not yet triaged: four cloned repositories deferred for grading (among them a pre-registered study with rewired controls), 13 sweep repositories and 12 new Fly Brain Hub links, and about 211 repositories listed only in directories.

Why the Shiu v783 file has 616 fewer neurons than the FlyWire v783 release is not established; the scope of BANC's "approximately 188,000 neurons" is not stated. The attractor reported for the Shiu et al. model has not been reproduced by us.

The Build your own guide is untested on macOS, Windows/WSL, Colab and machines with a C++ compiler; GitHub Pages publishing is untested. Add a body is tested on Linux CPU only, without rendering. DOOMFLY's and DesktopFly's run steps are untested by us.
FlyWire data licence conflict: CC BY-NC 4.0 in the official guidelines vs CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo v783 record; we follow the stricter, non-commercial reading.
Video summaries rest on titles, descriptions, captions, code and thumbnails; we did not watch every video frame by frame. View counts are snapshots.

Videos cannot play inside the site: YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and X players failed in the site's sandboxed frames (tested in headless Chromium only). YouTube and X thumbnails are loaded from their image servers.

Download facts: sizes are the hosts' own storage figures on 6 Oct 2026; MANC (bucket not listed) and larva L1 (supplement unreachable) sizes are not stated; the FlyWire Codex download page needs a sign-in and was not read; the hemibrain flat file is v1.2 while neuPrint serves v1.2.1.
Our environment test: one Linux machine, Python 3.12.11; Brian2 2.10.x with numpy 2.5 was not tested. A coupled brain-and-body test is not yet tested.
